tagline: What fire does to good meat.
sector: Food and beverage: a wood fired neighbourhood grill serving walk-in trade and delivery, opening a second room.
founded_place_size: A single-room wood fired grill on the west side of Providence, Rhode Island, opening its second room in launch week, run by a small owner-operator team.
about: Ember and Oak is a wood fired grill on the west side of Providence, one hearth you can see from every table, mains around thirty four dollars. Launch week opens the second room. The brand is fire, char and appetite: warm, loud and alive, built to make somebody hungry in the first two seconds.
audience: Walk-in diners on the west side deciding in the time it takes to scroll past, plus delivery orders. Neighbourhood people who want a room that feels alive, not a tasting menu and not a value grill.
price_positioning: A casual premium wood fired grill, mains around thirty four dollars. The grade runs warm, the cut is fast, the food fills the frame and the type is bold and immediate. Never moody fine dining, never a discount grill with a deal burned across the frame.

palette.name: Charcoal
palette.usage: The ink of the mark, as in emberoak_mark.png; a solid ground for closing cards and type panels, carrying Cream type and the mark in Cream; and the type and mark colour on Flame Yellow grounds, as type_system step 02 sets (Charcoal on Flame Yellow), and on Cream grounds, as emberoak_mark.png sets the mark.

palette.name: Ember Orange
palette.role: mandatory wherever a dish name is set
palette.usage: The solid 12 px hot bar behind the baseline of every dish name's lower line, the type_system signature move; otherwise only thin rules or dividers. Never type, a ground or a panel.

palette.name: Flame Yellow
palette.usage: A solid closing-card ground or type panel carrying Charcoal type and the mark in Charcoal, as type_system step 02 sets (Charcoal on Flame Yellow). Never a type colour.

palette.name: Oak Brown
palette.usage: Thin rules and dividers only. Never type, a ground or a panel.

palette.name: Cream
palette.role: mandatory where type or the mark sits on Charcoal or directly on footage; optional ground
palette.usage: Type and the mark reversed out of Charcoal, as type_system step 02 sets (Cream on Charcoal), and any type set directly on footage. Also a solid ground for a closing card or panel carrying the mark and type in Charcoal, as emberoak_mark.png sets them; never under a price or room line. The cream square baked into emberoak_mark.png is never carried over as part of the mark.

palette.name: Char Red
palette.usage: Thin rules and dividers only. Never type, a ground or a panel.

typography: Ember and Oak runs on two faces. Dish names set in Red Hat Display Black capitals at 112 px on 120 px leading, tracked minus 0.020 em, always over two lines, with a 12 px Ember Orange bar burning behind the baseline of the lower line and stopping flush with its final letter. Under it the price and room line sets in Atlas Grotesk Bold at 56 px on 62 px, tracked minus 0.010 em. Descriptions set in Atlas Grotesk Regular at 34 px on 44 px with tracking at zero and no more than 65 characters a line, and fine print such as hours and delivery sets in Atlas Grotesk Regular at 22 px on 30 px, tracked plus 0.030 em. Printed menus and window cards hold the same relationship at 34 pt names and 10 pt body on 14 pt. A dish name is never set in lowercase.
voice: Warm, direct, hungry. Short lines with heat in them. Example line the brand would write: 'The chop, the char, the fire you can see from your table. Second room now open.'
brand_assets_status: The mark survives only as a small raster: a two word lockup inside a thin ring, sitting on a cream square baked into the picture rather than behind it. It has to be recovered as clean, placeable artwork before it can go on the end card or the window poster.
values: Appetite and honesty: show the real food from the real service, and make the room feel like what it is. The reel should read like the room smells.

type_system.signature_move: The hot bar. Every dish name sets in Red Hat Display Black capitals over two lines at 112 px on 120 px, tracked minus 0.020 em, with a 12 px Ember Orange bar burning behind the baseline of the lower line and stopping flush with its final letter, so the name always looks like it is resting on something hot. That bar is the first thing a viewer sees.
rules: Never set a dish name in lowercase.
Every dish name breaks over two lines; the Ember Orange bar sits behind the baseline of the lower line only and stops flush with its last letter, never running past it.
The bar is 12 px deep at the 112 px screen size and scales with the name, never with the frame.
Dish names always track minus 0.020 em; no other step may borrow that tracking.
In print, dish names set 34 pt and body 10 pt on 14 pt.
Never let the type go moody fine dining, and never burn a discount deal across the frame.

palette_rules.distribution: Grounds and panels are Charcoal, Flame Yellow or Cream, and every closing card has one of them as a solid ground. Type and the mark are Cream on Charcoal and Charcoal on Flame Yellow, as type_system step 02 sets, and Charcoal on Cream, as emberoak_mark.png sets the mark; type set directly on footage is Cream. A price or room line sits only on a solid Charcoal or Flame Yellow panel (type_system step 02), never on Cream or directly on footage. Ember Orange is the hot bar behind every dish name and is never type, a ground or a panel. Beyond the hot bars, Ember Orange, Oak Brown and Char Red are accents for thin rules and dividers only, together no more than 5% of the designed, non-footage area.
palette_rules.opacity: Every palette colour is used solid, at 100% opacity. No tint, transparency, gradient, glow, shadow, outline or blend mode is applied to any palette colour, type, bar or the mark, and no scrim, vignette, gradient or overlay of any colour, black and white included, is laid over footage or a still: type that needs separation from the footage sits on a solid panel in the colours the distribution rule sets. A colour grade applied to the footage itself is not an overlay. Cuts and dissolves between shots are transitions, not tints; colour and opacity are judged on a settled frame.
palette_rules.forbidden: No colour outside the six palette hexes for type, bars, panels, rules, buttons or icons, and no discount or deal flash, badge or burst in any colour, which the type rules forbid.
palette_rules.photography: Footage and stills keep their own colour under the warm grade the brand positioning sets. A warm colour grade is allowed; a flat palette-colour overlay, tint or duotone that replaces their own colours is not. No detail is painted, generated or extended into footage or stills.
